patterns: is freestyle the same as front crawl
entries.answer: Freestyle in competitive swimming means any stroke other than breaststroke, and it is the fastest because the body is flat and the kick is small, so less energy goes into resistance. What most people picture as freestyle is actually front crawl, and the two are treated as the same event in competition. The rule that trips up beginners is that you may change stroke freely, so a swimmer can switch mid-length and it still counts as freestyle, which is why records are set on efficiency.

patterns: what is a lane in swimming
why are there ropes in a pool
how many lanes in a pool
entries.answer: A lane is one of the marked strips a swimmer travels down, and in a pool there are usually eight, six or ten, separated by floating ropes rather than walls. The ropes matter because they reduce what is called wave reflection, so a swimmer in a middle lane is not badly penalised by the splashing of the swimmers either side. In open water there are no lanes at all, which changes strategy completely since you cannot see who is ahead.

patterns: why do swimmers push off the rope
entries.answer: The lane rope is the floating barrier that separates one swimmer from the next, and it is there to absorb waves rather than to stop a determined swimmer from crossing. Swimmers push off it deliberately at every turn, which is why turning technique involves a flick rather than a stop, and crossing between lanes mid-race is a disqualification. Modern ropes are made of small discs threaded on a cable, which lets water through and takes the reflection out of the wave.

patterns: what is a turn in swimming
how do you turn in a pool
entries.answer: A turn is how a swimmer reverses at the wall, and it is worth several tenths of a second per length, which over a distance adds up to more than the margin between most finalists. There are two kinds: the somersault, used in freestyle, and the flip turn, identical in effect but named differently by stroke. What makes a turn fast is the wall being used, with a foot planted and the body folded, so the wall pushes back instead of the water stopping the swimmer.

entries.answer: Breaststroke is the slowest competitive stroke and the only one where the head must rise to breathe, and that constraint is why it is slow and also why it is the stroke most often taught first. The kick is called a frog kick because both legs draw up together, and the arms pull from beneath the surface. It is also the only stroke that cannot be performed continuously without breaking the surface, which is exactly why the breathing rhythm is the whole skill.
